antiqueTemple.pour_qui: Choose The Ancient Temple when you have been carrying too much and need a place that feels safe. This gentle rain meditation, lit by candles, suits a rainy evening or the end of a long week. Its 19 minutes fit easily into a quiet half hour. If sacred places and their timeless calm move you, this world is for you.
antiqueTemple.deroule: You climb worn stone steps through rain and mist, behind a white fox with nine glowing tails. A huge carved door opens under your gentle hand, and inside, hundreds of candles glow among giant stone Buddhas. An old guardian in a smiling wooden mask gives you a small candle. Then comes a candle meditation, guided by the guardian: each lamp you light wakes a painted legend. In a hall of floating candles, your candle can carry one weight away. This is a letting go meditation in a single gesture: you open your hand, and the candle rises. A wooden bodhisattva opens its eyes and shows you the night the temple was built. Behind a small red door lies your own inner landscape, and dawn turns everything gold.
conseils: Sit on a cushion on the floor, like the monks in the temple, and let your body grow heavy.
Before you press play, choose the one weight you would like your candle to carry away.
Afterwards, let Resonance, the singing bowl sound, play for ten minutes in Timed Ambience.
If immersive meditation is new to you, do not try to see every detail: a vague outline of the temple is enough.
faq: What is the small candle for?
The guardian gives it to you to light a row of old lamps, and each one wakes a moving painting. Later, in a hall of floating candles, you can let it carry one weight up into the air.
Do I need to be Buddhist to enjoy this world?
No need. The Buddhas and the wooden bodhisattvas are part of the scenery. If you bow, it is a simple greeting rather than worship, and you can skip it.
What is behind the small red door?
No gold and no jewels, but a wide landscape from your inner world, perhaps a calm sea or hills under snow. It is the heart of the temple, and the guardian lets you open it yourself.
Is the white fox a spirit animal?

You can see it that way. The nine-tailed fox comes from East Asian legends. As a fox spirit animal, it is often read as a sign of wit and gentle guidance. Here, it simply leads you up the steps to the temple.
Can I light a real candle?
Yes, if it is safe where you sit. Gazing at the flame for a minute is a simple candle flame meditation. Then close your eyes and let this Buddhist candle meditation take over.
Is there throat singing in the temple?
Yes, softly, beneath the rain and the old bell. Khoomei, a deep style of throat singing from Central Asia, hums in the background. It makes the visit a quiet throat singing meditation.
Is this a sacred space meditation?

Yes, in a simple way. The whole temple is a sacred space where nothing is asked of you, and no one asks who you are. At its heart, behind a small red door, the sanctuary holds a landscape of your own. You can return to it whenever you wish, which is what a sacred space meditation is for.
Do I hear a temple bell during the meditation?

Yes, once. While you sit among the stone Buddhas, an old bell rings outside in the mist, and lotus flowers light up as its note passes. Later, a wooden statue shows you the night the temple was built, when that same bell rang for the very first time.

cosmicTemple.pour_qui: When your thoughts feel small and crowded, The Cosmic Temple opens up space. At 13 minutes, it is one of the three shortest worlds, so it fits a quiet evening or a short break. This celestial meditation carries a vast, almost sacred calm. It suits you well when a question is on your mind.
cosmicTemple.deroule: You rise gently above the world into a warm violet dark, where a white marble temple floats. A celestial whale, huge as a hill, carries you around it on her back, then gives you a crystal sphere with a tiny galaxy inside. Within the temple, the marble turns clear as water above the stars. You turn the silver hand of a great golden clock and watch a distant people draw a sign in the sand. That sign becomes the circle of light where you sit, feeling as vast as the cosmos, while a star is born beneath you. In the end, only your sphere's golden glow remains.
conseils: Lie on your back and open your hands a little, as the session invites you to. An immersive meditation works best when the body has nothing left to do.
Prepare a short question before you start: you can let it rise like a star.
Afterwards, Nebula in Timed Ambience keeps this cosmos meditation going for a few minutes.
If this world makes you curious about spiritual awakening, the Cosmic & Void category goes further, with two sessions of about half an hour.
faq: Who carries me to the temple?
A celestial whale the size of a hill, with stars shining on her skin. She sets you down at the threshold and leaves you a crystal sphere with a tiny galaxy inside.
What happens at the heart of the temple?
You sit in a great circle of light, the very sign you saw drawn in the sand. Beneath you, a cloud of dust gathers with your breath until a star is born. It is the gentle peak of this star meditation.
Will I get an answer to my question?
The session does not promise one. Your question simply rises and turns into another star in the sky, which is a gentle way of letting it go.
Is the whale a spirit animal?
She can be, if you like. As for the whale spirit animal meaning, it usually points to depth, wisdom and calm strength. In this whale meditation, she carries you to the temple and leaves you a gift.
Is this a cosmic consciousness meditation?

You could call it that: for a moment, you feel as vast as the cosmos. There is no state to reach, only a deep and spacious calm. Like a light meditation, it ends in a circle of light and a golden glow.
Is this a cosmic energy meditation?
Not in the usual sense: there is no energy to channel or move. Instead, a star is born beneath your feet, and its first light warms your hands and face. You are the first to receive it.
Is there cosmic meditation music in this world?

Yes, as a soundscape rather than a melody. The session is carried by Nebula, a soft and spacious sound with a cosmic feel. Over it, you hear the low note of the cosmos, the song of the celestial whale and tiny stars that chime like glass. Afterwards, you can keep Nebula playing on its own in Timed Ambience, for up to an hour.

crystalCave.pour_qui: This crystal cave meditation suits the end of a heavy day. It helps when your head feels cluttered and you want to feel clear and light again. Its 17 minutes of immersive meditation are serene and full of small wonders. Choose it when you would rather rest in light and song than think things through, or simply when you love the hush of deep caves.
crystalCave.deroule: A sloping path leads you deep underground, where this crystal cave guided meditation begins. You slip through a narrow crack into an immense cavern of glowing crystals. A crystal butterfly guides you past still pools, where a mermaid sings one clear note. When you touch a tall crystal, the whole cave answers with a long chord, and what weighs on you lifts like mist. A boat no thicker than a soap bubble carries you to a little crystal dragon, which leads you to a tiny city of light. You sing softly with its people, then let a shade of light fill you before the crystals dim.
conseils: Listen in a dim room, so the crystal visualization glows more clearly in your mind.
When the tiny people sing, hum along softly if you like: words are not needed.
When a shade of light comes to you near the end, let it choose itself.
If you enjoy visualization meditation, the Visualization category trains the inner eye, one sense at a time.
faq: Who will I meet in the cave?
A crystal butterfly that guides you, a mermaid who sings one clear note and a little crystal dragon the size of a cat. The dragon leads you to a tiny city whose people are no taller than a finger.
Do I have to sing?
Only if you want to. The tiny people invite you to join their song very softly, even without words, and simply listening is fine too.
Is this world about emotions?
It is above all a clarity meditation: whatever weighs on you can lift away in the crystal light. You do not need to name or explain anything.
Do I need real crystals?
No. The crystals are all in your imagination, so there is nothing to buy or hold. If you wonder how to meditate with crystals, this is a gentle start: you simply rest in their light.
Is this a mermaid guided meditation?
In part. A mermaid sits by a still pool and sings one clear note for the cave. Later, you hear her note again in the song of the tiny people. Your guide, though, is a crystal butterfly.
How do you meditate with crystals?

The usual way is simple: hold a stone or set it in front of you, then rest your attention on its weight, its color and the light inside it. This world asks for no stone at all. You picture the crystals and rest in their glow. If you own one, you can hold it in your palm while you listen.
Is this crystal meditation good for beginners?

Yes. There is nothing to learn and nothing to hold. You follow a butterfly, listen to one clear note and let a shade of light come to you. If the pictures stay faint, the sounds carry you: echoing drops, singing crystals and soft chimes. A story can be easier to follow than silence when you are starting out.

galaxy.pour_qui: This galaxy meditation works well as a night meditation, when you need perspective and a sense of wonder. In 19 minutes, a train of light takes you past Saturn's rings to the far side of the galaxy and back. Choose it when something weighs on you, or for a starry night meditation that travels without moving.
galaxy.deroule: You float free of the ground until a golden train of light stops beside you. From your seat by the window, you watch a whale of light swim alongside, and one of your spirit guides quietly sits next to you. The train crosses the icy rings of Saturn and a shower of shooting stars, then stops at a glass station on an asteroid. In its night market, a merchant with golden eyes gives you a vial holding a tiny turning planet. Inside a glowing cloud, a short universe meditation lets you rest as a small, warm light. A ring of light folds space, and at the far end of the galaxy you let a weight pass through the glass. Then the train brings you home.
conseils: Sit in a comfortable armchair, like a passenger by the window, and let the galaxy visualization unfold: an immersive meditation asks for nothing more.
If you can, begin with a minute of stargazing meditation at a window or outside.
Afterwards, keep a small glass jar or bottle in view, like the merchant's vial, as a reminder of this calm.
If you enjoy a story meditation of this kind, The Unknown Planet, in the Mini Adventures category, lets you explore another world.
faq: What is the train of light?
A golden train that slides silently between the stars and picks you up where you float. It carries you past Saturn, a night market and a glowing nebula, then sets you down where it found you.
Who sits beside me on the train?
One of your guides, in whatever form comes to you: a face you know, or simply a soft glow. They say little, but seem to know the whole route.
What is the ring of light?
A passage that folds space. The train enters it and crosses the whole galaxy in a single breath, where heavy things suddenly feel small.
Can I use it as a space sleep meditation?

You can listen at night, and the slow train is very soothing. But this space guided meditation brings you back at the end, so it is not built for falling asleep. For bedtime, Drifting into Sleep ends with no wake-up.
Do I need to like science fiction?
Not at all. This outer space meditation feels more like a fairy tale than science fiction. Think of a golden train, a whale of light and a night market. You simply sit by the window and watch.
Is this a Saturn meditation?

Partly, since Saturn is one of its highlights. The train glides through the planet's icy rings, and ice taps the glass like pearls. Then come shooting stars, a night market and the far edge of the galaxy.
Is there a space meditation app with this journey?

Yes. Journey Through the Galaxy is one of the 17 immersive worlds in MeditaDream, a free app for iPhone and Android. There is no subscription, no ads and no account. Once the session is downloaded, it plays offline, so you can listen on a plane or far from any signal.

earthCore.pour_qui: Some days you feel scattered, rushed or a little up in the air. This grounding visualization invites you down toward something steady and ancient. As a 15-minute grounding meditation, it fits before a demanding meeting or at the start of a busy day. It will appeal to anyone who likes deep, primal places and gentle surprises. If you work with the chakras, this is root chakra territory: weight, steadiness and the ground beneath you.
earthCore.deroule: This immersive meditation begins as warm air breathes out of an opening in the rock, and a wide stone path leads you down. Crystal veins and emerald plants glow in vast caverns, and a wall brightens under your hand as if it were breathing. Rivers of orange light guide you into a hollow world lit by its own gentle sun. A giant butterfly leads you through a jungle to an amber egg resting among the roots of an immense tree. As you hold it, it beats with the Earth, and a small green dragon hatches. Glowing people offer you a word or an image, and a column of light lifts you home.
conseils: Sit with both feet flat on the floor, or barefoot on the ground if you can. It is one of the simplest earth grounding techniques.
Carry a smooth pebble in your pocket afterwards, as a small reminder of this steadiness.
If you like deep, low sounds, try Monolith, a drone, in Timed Ambience after the session.
Before you press play, you can try the 5-4-3-2-1 grounding technique: name five things you see, four you can touch, three you hear, two you smell and one you taste.
faq: What is at the heart of the Earth?

A hollow world as vast as a sky, with forests curving up all around and a soft sun floating in the middle. Its warm, golden light is gentle enough to look at directly. It feels like a Mother Earth meditation: warm, ancient and kind.
What hatches from the amber egg?
A little dragon with moss-green scales, no bigger than a cat. It sleeps against you in the warm sand, then stays below to grow up in the warmth.
Who lives in the hollow world?
Tall, slender beings whose skin glows like the moon, carrying balls of light. They speak without words and offer you a message to carry with you: one word, or an image.
Is this a good grounding meditation for beginners?
Yes. There is nothing to master: you follow a path down and let the Earth carry you. Sitting with your feet on the floor helps you feel grounded from the first minute.
What does grounding yourself to the earth mean?

It means feeling your weight, your contact with the ground and a sense of steadiness. In this world, the image becomes a journey: you travel down to the warm heart of the planet. It is an earth grounding meditation you do with your imagination.
What is grounding in meditation?

In meditation, grounding means bringing your attention back to the body and its contact with the ground: your weight, your feet, your breath. Many people use it when the mind races or they feel scattered. It has nothing to do with electricity, and it needs no equipment. This world offers an imaginative version, a slow journey down to the warm heart of the Earth.
Is there a 5-minute grounding meditation?

Not in this world, which lasts 15 minutes. For a short reset, the 4 Minutes category offers sessions of 3 to 4 minutes, such as Your Instant Refuge. You can also try the simplest grounding exercise there is: sit down, feel both feet on the floor and take three slow breaths. Then come back to The Heart of the Earth when you have a quarter of an hour.

antarcticBase.pour_qui: When the world feels too loud, The Frozen Sanctuary offers real silence. This winter guided meditation brings 15 minutes of stillness, solitude and a touch of mystery. Listen after a noisy day, or whenever you crave quiet. It is a small lesson in the power of silence. Lovers of polar landscapes, auroras and calm science fiction will feel at home in this ice meditation.
antarcticBase.deroule: You sink slowly through layers of ancient ice, past old stars caught inside. A polar fox with glowing fur waits at an opening carved by non-human hands, and leads you down a deep blue tunnel where symbols float. You only need to look at them. In a vast hall, frost flowers open as the fox walks by. You sit before a great crystal heart, letting each out-breath lay down what you carry. In an ice library, a book shows a white city from before the ice. Then an aurora guides you out under the open sky, and a white feather carries you home.
conseils: Wrap yourself in a blanket: the warmth makes the return from the ice even sweeter.
Choose a quiet room and turn off your notifications, since stillness is at the heart of this world. An immersive meditation like this one deserves fifteen minutes without interruption.
Remember the white feather afterwards: it is your way back to this place.
If the crystal heart stays with you, The Infinite Crystal Cave offers a full crystal cave meditation.
faq: Is The Frozen Sanctuary a science-fiction story?
Not really. It borrows the mystery of a sanctuary built long ago by beings who were not human, but it remains a calm, slow guided meditation.
Do I need to understand the floating symbols?
There is no need. Simply looking at them is enough, and the mind that always wants answers can take a rest.
What does the ice library show?
A book frees itself from the ice under your hand. Its pages show a white city from long before the ice, where calm, kind beings lived among red-furred mammoths.
Is the polar fox a spirit animal?

You can welcome it as one. The arctic fox spirit animal is often linked to quiet adaptability and finding your way in the cold. Here, it simply guides you through the ice, and you only need to follow.
Is this a snow meditation?
Partly. Most of the journey happens under the ice, in blue tunnels and frozen halls. At the end, a white feather carries you over the snow, under the aurora.
Is there an aurora in this meditation?

Yes. Near the end, a green glow comes down through the ceiling of ice, then a pink one. Night has fallen, and an aurora leads you up to the open sky. Over Antarctica, these are the southern lights. If you are looking for an aurora borealis meditation, The Wolf Spirit Forest takes place under the northern lights.
Can I use it as a winter solstice meditation?

Yes, it suits the longest night well. The descent passes through thousands of winters of ice, into a silence where nothing needs to happen. Then light returns, as an aurora fills the sanctuary. There is no ritual to follow. Wrap yourself in a blanket, dim the lights and let the quiet do the rest.

skyIsland.pour_qui: Everyone needs a place of their own. The Floating Island is yours, far from demands and noise. It suits the late afternoon or early evening, since its scene moves from a low orange sun to the first stars. Its 19 minutes make a floating meditation full of freedom and safety, like a private sanctuary above the clouds. Picturing a safe place is one of the best-known exercises in guided imagery, and this world turns it into a journey.
skyIsland.deroule: You spend this guided meditation floating high above the world. A bridge of clouds, soft as wool, leads you to a small green island. From its edge, you see forests like moss and cities lighting up far below. You sit by a waterfall that pours into the open sky. Then a great white and gold bird flies you to the ancient tree at the island's heart. A white stag with pearl wings, its guardian, gives you a shining seed. At sunset, a whale passes beneath the island and you set down what you carried. At nightfall, you blow on the seed, and a tiny island is born among the shooting stars.
conseils: Listen to this island meditation around sunset if you can, so the light outside matches the scene.
When the seed comes, hold it loosely in an open palm until evening.
Come back often: this inner sanctuary meditation is meant to stay your own refuge. Like any immersive meditation, it grows more familiar with each visit.
faq: How do I reach the island?
On a bridge of clouds that unrolls at your feet, soft as wool yet strong enough to hold you. It folds away behind you, then returns at nightfall to take you home.
What is the seed for?
The island's guardian, a white stag with pearl wings, gives you a shining seed of the great tree. At nightfall, you blow it from your hand toward the sky or the ocean, and a tiny island is born.
Does the session end at night?
It does. Evening falls, and the last minutes become a night sky meditation. Lanterns light up in the great tree and fireflies float by. Shooting stars cross the sky as you walk back over the bridge.
Is the white stag a spirit animal?
You can see it that way. The stag spirit animal is often linked to gentleness, dignity and renewal. Here, the winged white stag guards the island and gives you a shining seed.
Is this a floating-on-a-cloud meditation?
Almost. Your island drifts among soft clouds, and the world lies far below. In this cloud visualization, little flakes rise around you like dandelion fluff.
Is there a safe place visualization script I can use on my own?

Yes, and it takes only four steps. Close your eyes and picture a place where nothing is asked of you. Add what you see, what you hear and what you feel under your hands. Stay there for a few slow breaths. Then choose one detail to remember, so you can find the place again. The Floating Island guides you through a fuller version of the same exercise.

zenGarden.pour_qui: When everything moves too fast, this zen garden meditation invites you to slow down completely. It calls up the Zen beginner’s mind: seeing each petal and stone as if for the first time. This immersive meditation lasts 18 minutes and suits a quiet late afternoon, or any moment when you need balance. It will also speak to you if you love Japanese gardens, cherry blossoms and simple, elegant calm.
zenGarden.deroule: You step through a wooden gate into a Japanese garden just after the rain. A white fox with nine tails watches you pass, and a great cherry tree opens all its buds at once. From a little wooden bridge, you feed the koi, and the golden one brushes your hand. Then, in a short koi pond meditation, you watch the water hold the whole sky. A bamboo fountain taps against stone while you let your mind grow as still as the pond. An old gardener raking white sand shares tea with you, and its steam takes the shape of a dragon, then a phoenix. At dusk, stone lanterns light your way to a singing bamboo grove full of fireflies.
conseils: For a simple meditation posture, sit upright on a cushion or the edge of a chair, hands resting in your lap.
Let your breathing follow the slow tap of the bamboo fountain, without counting. Many zen breathing techniques simply follow the breath like this.
Take a short, slow walk afterwards to carry the pace of the stone path into your day. Zen walking meditation, called kinhin, is just that: slow steps and full attention.
faq: Do I walk or sit in the Zen Garden?
Both, in your imagination. You walk the stone path and stop on a little bridge. Later, you sit on a wooden terrace for tea, then on a flat stone among the bamboo.
Who is the old gardener?
A quiet old man who rakes the white sand in perfect lines and shares tea with you on a terrace. As he leaves, his shadow briefly shows nine tails, like the fox on the path.
Can I fit The Zen Garden into a lunch break?
Easily. This Japanese garden meditation lasts 18 minutes, which leaves time to settle in before and to stretch a little afterwards.
What is zen meditation?

Zen meditation comes from Zen Buddhism. Zazen meditation, its core practice, means sitting upright and letting thoughts pass. The history of Zen runs from China, where it was called Chan, to Japan. The Zen Garden is a guided visualization in that spirit, not a silent zazen session.
Is this a tea ceremony meditation?
Not a formal one. The old gardener simply pours you tea on a terrace, and you sip it slowly, like a tea meditation. If you like, make a real cup to drink afterwards.
Are there zen meditation techniques for beginners here?
Yes, in a gentle form. You sit upright, follow your breath and let the scenes pass without holding on. It is an easy first step before trying silent zazen on your own.
When does the cherry tree bloom?
Early on, just after the white fox. As you walk beneath its branches, every bud opens at once. For a few breaths, the session becomes a cherry blossom meditation, with petals falling all around you.
How do you do zen meditation?

Sit upright on a cushion or a chair, hands resting in your lap, eyes half open and lowered. Breathe naturally through the nose and count each out-breath from one to ten, then begin again. When thoughts come, let them pass and return to the count. Ten minutes is a good start. The Zen Garden offers the same spirit in a guided, visual form.
What is a Japanese zen garden?

A Japanese zen garden, or karesansui, is a dry garden of raked gravel, stones and moss, made to be contemplated from the outside rather than walked through. The best known lies at Ryoanji temple in Kyoto, with its fifteen stones. The garden in this world is more varied: around its raked white sand, it adds a koi pond, a cherry tree and a bamboo grove.

atlantis.pour_qui: If your feelings seem stuck and you would like them to move again, sink into this Atlantis meditation. Its 17 minutes are slow and fluid, and someone else does the swimming. Choose this sea meditation if you love the ocean, or whenever you want to rest in flow rather than effort. As an immersive meditation, it asks only one thing of you: let yourself be carried.
atlantis.deroule: You float on a warm sea, then sink gently and find that you can breathe underwater. Towers crowned with pink coral rise from an ancient city of pale temples. A giant golden seahorse carries you among them, past glowing fish and jellyfish that pulse like bells of light. A couple with moon-pale skin welcomes you into their round house and offers a drink that tastes of mint and honey. In their coral garden, a warm pearl shows you one of your memories. On a terrace of living coral, a distant whale sings as your feelings move and settle. At nightfall, the city lights up before the sea lifts you.
conseils: Lie down and let your arms rest loosely, as if they were floating.
Keep breathing at your own pace: in this ocean visualization, the water is only imagery.
To stay by the sea a little longer, play Ocean Waves in Timed Ambience for a short ocean waves meditation.
At bedtime, try Ocean Waves on its own: it is one of the sleep sounds you can play on a timer.
faq: Do I need to like swimming?
No swimming is needed in this ocean meditation. A giant golden seahorse carries you through the city, and you can even breathe underwater.
What is the pearl?
A warm, cherry-sized pearl, waiting in a shell in your hosts' garden. When you look into its glow, one of your memories comes back, and the pearl keeps it safe as you leave.
Is there a whale in Underwater Atlantis?
There is. While you rest on a terrace of living coral, a whale sings far away, then closer. Its long, low note seems to pass right through you.
Is the golden seahorse a spirit animal?
You can welcome it as one. The seahorse spirit animal is often linked to patience and calm protection, as in most seahorse symbolism. Here, it carries you gently between the coral towers.
Is it a deep sea meditation?
Not a dark one. The sea stays warm and full of light, with glowing fish and jellyfish that pulse like bells. You rest deep below the surface, yet everything feels gentle.
How is it different from an ocean guided meditation?

Many ocean meditations keep you on the shore, listening to the waves. This underwater guided meditation takes you below the surface, where you breathe freely among coral towers. The Ocean Waves sound still plays in the background.
What is Atlantis?

Atlantis first appears in two dialogues by the Greek philosopher Plato, the Timaeus and the Critias, written around 360 BC. He describes a great island power that sank into the sea in a single day and night. Most scholars read it as a story with a moral, not as history. In this world, Atlantis is simply a peaceful city resting under the sea.

himalayanMonastery.pour_qui: Monastery at Sunrise is a guided morning meditation. Listen as your day begins, when you want clarity before what lies ahead. This Himalayan meditation also suits a decision or a fresh start, at any hour. Mountain lovers will find their place here, among prayer flags and snowy peaks. So will anyone curious about Tibetan meditation.
himalayanMonastery.deroule: It begins in the blue hour before dawn, outside a monastery high in the mountains, under the last stars. A smiling monk in a red robe welcomes you with a butter lamp. He leads you through a frosted garden, where you turn a prayer wheel. In a courtyard of prayer flags, you send a kind thought for someone you love with the wind horse. On a wooden balcony, he hands you a bowl of tea and tells how the monastery began with a single lamp. Then the sun rises over the peaks, the snow turns pink and gold, and a snow lion appears on a ridge as the valley wakes.
conseils: Listen to this sunrise meditation soon after waking, before you check your messages. It can anchor a morning meditation routine: same seat, same window, same hour.
Sit facing a window, so the morning light reaches your face: real light makes an immersive meditation even more vivid.
If you can, open the window for a breath of cool, fresh air.
If the old monk makes you curious about Buddhist meditation, the Buddhist Meditations category follows the bodhisattvas in longer journeys.
faq: Should I only listen in the morning?
Morning is the natural fit, since the session follows a sunrise. You can still play it later in the day: the scene brings its own dawn.
Who guides me through the monastery?

An old monk, robed in dark red and carrying a butter lamp. He pours you tea on a wooden balcony and tells the story of the first visitor, whose lamp has never gone out. Walking beside him is a gentle Tibetan monk meditation: slow steps, a prayer wheel, a kind thought.
How long does the sunrise last?
This monastery meditation lasts 18 minutes, from the last stars before dawn to full sunlight over the valley. It is a free morning meditation, and it plays offline once downloaded.
What do the prayer flags mean?

In Tibetan Buddhism, prayer flags carry wishes of peace on the wind. The prayer flags' meaning is simple: each gust spreads kindness to all. In the session, you send a kind thought for someone you love.
Is this a Tibetan Buddhist meditation?
It borrows its setting and its gestures, from the butter lamp to the prayer wheel. You need no belief and no ritual to follow it. At its heart are a kind thought and the rising sun.
What is mountain meditation?

In its classic form, taught in many mindfulness courses, mountain meditation asks you to picture a mountain and then become it: steady through every season and every kind of weather. This guided mountain meditation takes another path to the same calm. You sit facing snowy peaks at dawn and wait patiently, like the mountain, until the sunlight comes down to meet you.

celestialLibrary.pour_qui: The Celestial Library is for quiet, reflective moments, when you want to turn something over in your mind, without hurry. Its 13 minutes make it one of the three shortest worlds: an immersive meditation that fits an evening at home, a pause before writing or a short break. It is a good match for curious minds and for anyone who loves old libraries and starry ceilings.
celestialLibrary.deroule: A tall wooden door opens onto a library without end, where candles float between the shelves and books fly to the readers who need them. A candle leads you up a spiral staircase to a gallery of books from vanished worlds. In a silver book, you meet a gentle people who grow their gardens by singing. In an old armchair under the stars, a fire salamander made of golden light curls against your arm. A golden book without words then shows a picture of what could be, and nothing is forced. On your way out, the salamander leaves a small golden key in your hand.
conseils: Before you begin, pick an area of your life that feels important at the moment.
Afterwards, note what came to you in Spiritual Experiences, the app's own spiritual journal.
Listen by the light of a single soft lamp, like the candles of the library. A dim room helps this library visualization take shape.
For a longer journey into the Akashic records themselves, try The Keeper of the Archives, in the Higher Knowledge & Beyond category.
faq: What do the books show?
Two of them open for you. A silver book reveals a vanished world with two moons, and a golden book with no words shows one possible picture of your path ahead.
What if no picture comes?
That is fine, and the session says so itself. Sometimes a weight lifts instead, and if nothing comes, you just hold the warm book.
Is it the same as The Infinite Library?
No. The Infinite Library is a separate 32-minute session in the Consciousness & Trance category. The Celestial Library is one of the 17 immersive worlds and lasts 13 minutes.
Is this the Akashic records library?
It is inspired by it. In spiritual traditions, the Akashic records library holds the memory of every soul. Here it becomes a calm, starry place to explore, with no belief required.
What is the Akashic library?

In modern spiritual writing, the Akashic library, or Akashic records, is pictured as a universal library that holds every life, thought and event. The word comes from the Sanskrit akasha, meaning sky or space. Theosophists spread the idea in the late nineteenth century. It is a belief rather than an established fact, and this world simply borrows its image: a calm library without end.

h2.deroule: What happens in the Akashic library?

desertOasis.pour_qui: This desert meditation is for evenings when you need solitude and a little distance from the world. It offers a calm, safe space to be with what you feel. Its 13 minutes begin at sunset and end by a fire under the moon. It is a true meditation under the stars, for anyone who loves wide skies. Although it is not a sleep meditation, it suits the last quiet hour of the day.
desertOasis.deroule: In this guided visualization, you walk over warm dunes at sunset as the first stars appear. A spirit of golden sand rises and calls a white camel, which carries you to an oasis glowing between palm trees. In a night market, an old merchant pours mint tea and lets you have a small lamp for a smile. Glowing butterflies fly out of it and lead you to a pool that opens like glass onto a hidden garden and an old Egyptian temple. Back by a small fire, under an immense moon, you may share one true thing with the night, or stay silent.
conseils: Listen after dark, with the lights off or very low, as for a moonlight meditation.
Make yourself a cup of mint tea, like the one the old merchant pours.
If a feeling is there, let it be, without looking for a name.
Give this immersive meditation a quiet quarter of an hour: it lasts 13 minutes, which leaves a moment to linger in the calm afterwards.
faq: Do I have to speak out loud?
Not unless you want to. You may share one true thing with the night, silently or in a whisper, and saying nothing at all is just as welcome.
What is in the old lamp?
No genie, but glowing butterflies. They lead you to the pool and down to a hidden garden, then return to the lamp, which you keep.
Is The Desert Oasis only for difficult feelings?
Not at all. Whatever you feel can simply be there, without a name. Much of the journey is pure wonder: a camel ride, a night market and a hidden garden.
Is it a moon meditation?
In a way. The journey ends by a small fire under an immense moon. There, you may share one true thing with the night. Its silver light stays with you as you leave.
Is this a full moon meditation?

It can be one. At the end, an enormous moon turns the dunes silver, and you are invited to set down whatever you carry beside the water. There is no ritual and nothing to wish for. On a full moon night, listen by a window. It also works as a new moon meditation, when the sky is at its darkest.

h2.qui: Is this oasis meditation for you?

treeOfConsciousness.pour_qui: Reach for this oneness meditation when you feel cut off and want to feel part of something larger. At 18 minutes, it fits easily into an evening pause, and its glowing forest makes it a gentle night meditation. Immersive from start to finish, this guided tree meditation suits anyone who feels at home among trees, roots and living things.
treeOfConsciousness.deroule: The tree of life visualization begins in a glowing forest at night. You walk to an immense tree whose branches reach up among the stars. Under your hand, the bark beats slowly. Its guardian, made of wood and moss, steps out of the trunk and takes your hand. For a moment, you feel every living thing on Earth beating together. You climb a staircase of roots past the tree's memories and walk along branches as wide as bridges. A glass-winged butterfly brings you a leaf that holds a tiny, kind world. Finally you sit at the foot of the tree, leaning on its warm trunk, the leaf pressed to your heart.
conseils: Sit with your back against a wall, or against a real tree outdoors for a grounding tree meditation.
Near the end of the tree visualization, rest one hand on your heart, as if holding the leaf.
Listen in the evening if you can, since the forest glows at night.
Looking for a Bodhi tree meditation instead? Beneath the Bodhi Tree, in the Sacred Places category, lasts 17 minutes.
faq: Who steps out of the tree?
A tall figure of moss and wood, with leafy hair and golden eyes. He steps out of the bark, takes your hand and shows you how every life on Earth is connected.
What is inside the leaf?
A whole little world, with rivers between hills of moss and a little town built of pale wood and flower petals. There, people look after one another.
What does life energy mean here?
It is an image: a soft warmth climbing through you, like sap in a tree. You do not need to feel anything special for this tree of life guided meditation to be worthwhile.
What does the tree of life symbolize?

Tree of life symbolism appears in many cultures, from Norse myth to Celtic art. With roots in the earth and branches in the sky, it stands for the bond between all living things. The session lets you feel that bond rather than study it.
Do I need to know the tree of life spiritual meaning?
Not at all. Many traditions speak of a tree of life, meaning one life shared by all beings. You need no belief here: simply follow the guardian up the roots.
Is this a Kabbalah tree of life meditation?

No. In Kabbalah, the Tree of Life is a diagram of ten spheres, the sefirot, and its meditations follow that map. This world is not based on it. Its tree is closer to the world trees of myth: roots in the earth, branches among the stars and one life flowing through everything. No knowledge of any tradition is needed.

jungleRuins.pour_qui: This rainforest meditation is for the explorer in you. Choose it when you feel restless and want something to be curious about, while staying calm. This immersive meditation rewards a slow afternoon, ideally on a warm or rainy day. It lasts 18 minutes, a tropical meditation for anyone drawn to lost cities and green, mysterious places.
jungleRuins.deroule: Mist parts on a warm jungle to reveal a whole city asleep beneath ancient trees. You climb a mossy staircase through the ruins, and glowing insects gather into a small monkey of light. By a waterfall, a water spirit lays her cool hand on yours. A spiral carved in the wall lights up under your finger. Then a well leads down to a calm ocean beneath the city, where you can breathe, as in an underwater meditation. Great, peaceful creatures guide you to a garden of glowing flowers that hold old memories. Back in the courtyard, you plant a seed that grows into a tree, and a warm rain begins.
conseils: Let your curiosity lead this guided visualization: notice details without needing to explain them.
Afterwards, any tree branch you see can bring this place back to mind.
The session ends as rain begins, so let After Rain, one of the app's sleep sounds, play on in Timed Ambience.
faq: Is the thunder loud?
Far from it. It rolls only once, soft and low, far away in the jungle, and then fades.
Who is the little monkey?
A guide made of light, born from the glowing insects, with stardust fur and golden eyes. A water spirit also joins you for a moment by the waterfall.
What are the glowing symbols?
Spirals and wave shapes carved along an old wall, which light up under your fingertip. Deep below the city, you discover where the very first spiral was carved.
What will I hear in this jungle sounds meditation?
Falling water, humming insects and, near the end, a warm rain. Deep below the city, great creatures sing softly under the water. Everything stays soft, so it suits a quiet room.
Is there a waterfall in this rainforest guided meditation?
Yes. A clear waterfall pours through a gap in the old stone, into a quiet pool. For a full waterfall guided meditation, try The Body Under a Waterfall, in the Body, Calm & Sleep category.
Can I use the jungle sounds for sleep?

Not the session itself, which brings you back at the end. If you want jungle sounds for sleep, play After Rain on its own in Timed Ambience. It is a real recording of rain falling on a rainforest. Choose 5 to 60 minutes, and the sound fades out gently when the time is up.

h2.qui: Who is this jungle meditation for, and when?

mushroomForest.pour_qui: This fantasy meditation is pure play: a place to imagine and escape for a while. Try it during a creative break, on a lazy weekend afternoon or on an evening when classic meditation feels too serious. Its 17 minutes invite wonder and free imagination. This magical forest meditation is especially fun if you love fairy tales. It is not forest bathing among real trees: here, the mushrooms glow and the trees bear galaxies.
mushroomForest.deroule: This enchanted forest guided meditation drops you straight into a dream. It is an immersive meditation with no journey to make: you are already there. Around you rises a warm forest of giant glowing mushrooms, painted purple and pink. A tiny fairy lands on your hand, and a moss path lights up beneath your steps. From a silver tree, you pick a little galaxy, watch its whole life unfold and receive a word from its heart. A river of light chimes like small bells, with gentle creatures drifting above it. Butterflies of light show you an image of yourself living a dream you care about. Then a huge octopus of soft light lifts you above the forest, before everything gently fades.
conseils: Let this forest visualization be strange: there is nothing to understand.
Settle somewhere soft, such as a sofa or a bed, for a deep forest relaxation.
To stretch out the storybook mood, play Fairy Tale in Timed Ambience afterwards.
If you enjoy a story meditation, the Mini Adventures category offers four more tales, from a train of memories to an unknown planet.
faq: Are there creatures in the Dream Forest?
Plenty: a tiny fairy, gentle creatures like jellyfish of light and a huge octopus that carries you over the forest. From up there, you see crystal-antlered deer come to drink.
What is the word from the galaxy?
You pick a little galaxy from a silver tree and watch its whole life in a few breaths. A word then rises from its heart, and you take it home with you.
Is it a sleep meditation?
No, it is a dreamlike, magical meditation: at the end you come back lighter, with a sense of wonder. For bedtime, Drifting into Sleep ends with no wake-up.
Is this a fairy meditation?
In part. Early on, a tiny fairy lands on your hand, lighter than a feather. The rest is a fantasy guided meditation, with a galaxy to pick and an octopus of light to ride.
How do I do a forest visualization if I cannot picture things clearly?

You do not need sharp pictures. Start with one sense: the warm moss under you, the smell of rain or the low hum of the forest. Then let one detail appear, such as a single blue mushroom. The session keeps offering sounds and colors, so a faint impression is enough.
Is it the same as forest bathing?

No. Forest bathing, or shinrin-yoku, is a slow walk among real trees, with your senses open. The Dream Forest is pure imagination, with glowing mushrooms and silver trees. For a short taste of the real practice, try Shinrin-Yoku, a 6-minute session in the World Meditations category.

mirrorDimension.pour_qui: This mirror meditation is for the curious meditator who wants to look at awareness itself. Like an open awareness meditation, it helps you step back from your thoughts and watch them from a distance. That simple step back is one of the core self-awareness skills. This immersive meditation moves from still mirrors to small dreamlike worlds and back in 16 minutes, so it suits a quiet room where no one will disturb you.
mirrorDimension.deroule: You float, weightless, in soft white light among endless mirrors, while a pure tone sings far off. A fairy of water and silver swims through the glass, showing your thoughts how to pass. Then one mirror shows an animal instead of you: your guide, a spirit animal of your own. You follow it through the glass into rain that rises, a honey sky full of tiny worlds and still water you can walk on. At an old round mirror, you can leave behind a difficult moment, seen very small, and receive a pearl of light. Finally your own calm face appears, and you rest as the one who is looking.
conseils: Sit upright with your eyes closed, and let your body feel as light as possible.
As in witness meditation, see each thought as one more reflection, then let it pass.
If guided awareness meditation is new to you, start with Observing Thoughts, a meditation for beginners in the Learning Basics category.
For a real mirror meditation afterwards, sit in front of a mirror for two minutes and meet your own eyes with the same kind gaze.
faq: Will I see my own reflection?

Not at first: the first still mirror shows an animal, your guide. It is the moment you meet your spirit animal, maybe an owl, a fox or a deer. Your own face comes near the end, looking back with kind eyes that judge nothing.
What happens at the round mirror?
If you wish, you hand it a difficult moment, seen very small, without reliving it. A pearl of warm light comes back, holding what that moment taught you, without its weight.
What does resting as awareness mean?

It means noticing what in you observes your thoughts as they come and go, and staying there instead of following them. Some teachers call it witnessing awareness. Others speak of witness consciousness meditation, or awareness of awareness meditation.
Is this a “Who am I?” meditation?
Close to it. The question here is “who is looking?”, the heart of any self inquiry meditation. You do not need to answer it: you simply rest as the one who looks.
Is this a mirror gazing meditation?
Not quite. Classic mirror gazing uses a real mirror and your own eyes. Here the mirrors are imagined, and your own face only appears near the end, calm and kind.
Is this a spirit animal meditation?
Partly. Your animal guide leads you from mirror to mirror, through small dreamlike worlds. But the heart of the journey is a question: who is looking?
What is self-awareness meditation?

It is any practice in which you turn your attention toward your own mind. You notice thoughts, feelings and reactions as they appear, instead of being carried off by them. Most forms use the breath or the body as an anchor. The Mirror Dimension uses images instead: each thought becomes a reflection, and you learn to rest as the one who sees it.
Is this a self-reflection meditation?

In both senses of the word. You move among reflections, and you watch how your own mind works: thoughts pass like images over a mirror, and something in you sees them. There is nothing to analyze during the session. If you like to reflect in writing afterwards, the app has journals for that.

h2.qui: Who is this self-awareness meditation for, and when?
h2.conseils: Tips for this guided awareness meditation

wolfForest.pour_qui: This power animal meditation is for times when you need to feel protected and guided. Listen before a challenge, a difficult conversation or a step you are unsure about. Its 15 minutes invite you back to your instinct and a quiet kind of strength. Snowy forests, wild animals and the northern lights set the scene for this immersive meditation.
wolfForest.deroule: At the edge of a blue pine forest, under an enormous moon, you step onto fresh snow. A transparent wolf full of stars appears on the path, and snowdrops light up under its paws. A whole pack gathers, forms a circle and welcomes you, while your wolf spirit guide rests its forehead against yours. You run with them, faster and lighter, until you become a starry wolf yourself and howl at the moon. The northern lights form a bridge up to the icy ring of a giant planet. Back in a clearing, you sit by a sacred fire beside your wolf and keep its calm strength.
conseils: Listen to this wolf spirit meditation in the evening, lights low, so the moonlit forest feels close.
Let the wolf beside you take shape slowly, in as much detail as you like.
When the pack howls, breathe out long and slow, as if your own howl were rising.
If meeting a power animal speaks to you, the Shamanic Trance category goes further, with a full shamanic journey in each session.
faq: Are the wolves frightening?
Quite the opposite. They are wolf spirits, transparent and full of stars, who keep their distance until they welcome you as one of the pack. This wolf meditation stays gentle from start to finish.
Do I really become a wolf?
In your imagination, yes. As you run with the pack, your hands turn into paws and your fur fills with stars. By the fire, your body becomes your own again.
Will I see the northern lights?

You will, as the journey turns into a northern lights meditation. After the pack howls, ribbons of green and blue light, the aurora borealis, gather into a bridge. You run along it, up to the icy ring of a giant planet.
What does the wolf symbolize?

Wolf symbolism often speaks of loyalty, family and quiet strength. In shamanic traditions, a power animal, wolf or bear, guides you through the dark. Here, the wolf spirit animal meaning becomes something you feel, running with a pack of starry wolves.
Is the wolf my animal totem?

It can be, if it speaks to you. Many people see a wolf animal totem as a sign of trust in their own instinct. The session leaves the wolf totem meaning open: you simply keep the calm strength of your wolf.
What are the traits of a wolf spirit animal?

People who feel close to the wolf often name the same traits: loyalty to a small circle, strong instincts and a need for both company and solitude. Treat them as a mirror rather than a label. In the session, they take a simple form: a pack that welcomes you, a run through the snow and a quiet strength you keep.
How do I know what my spirit animal is?

There is no test to pass. Notice which animal keeps coming back in your dreams, your memories or your thoughts, and how you feel when you picture it. In this world, see what happens when the pack welcomes you: if it feels like coming home, the wolf may be yours. If another animal comes to mind instead, The Mirror Dimension lets your own guide appear.
